questions.stem: The function of the Golgi tendon organ is to _________

options.label: C
options.text: Sense changes in position of the muscle

options.label: D
options.text: Sense changes in length of the muscle

questions.solutionHtml:
Golgi tendon organ sense changes in muscle tension.

Golgi tendon reflex (Inverse myotatic/ Inverse stretch reflex) is disynaptic, is the opposite of the stretch reflex.

When the tension in a contracted muscle is significantly elevated, the inhibitory effect from the Golgi tendon organ leads to instantaneous relaxation of the entire muscle. This effect is called the lengthening reaction.

It is a protective mechanism to prevent tearing of the muscle or avulsion of the tendon from its attachments to the bone.



Note: Muscle spindles senses changes in muscle length (stretch).







Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition, Page nos 228 and 229

questions.stem: Pacemaker generating the rhythm for breathing is ________

options.label: B
options.text: Dorsal group of neurons in the medulla

questions.solutionHtml:
Pre-Botzinger complex generates the rhythm for automated breathing.

  • These are also known as pacemaker cells located in the medulla.
  • These are the first set of neurons that initiate inspiration.
  • These neurons discharge rhythmically, and they produce rhythmic discharges in the phrenic motor neurons.

Breathing is under the control of both the following:

  • Voluntary control: Located in the cerebral cortex (via corticospinal tract)
  • Automatic control: Driven by pacemaker cells in the medulla (Pre-Botzinger complex). These activate motor neurons via cervical (Phrenic nerve innervating diaphragm) and thoracic spinal cord (external intercostal muscle).

There is a reciprocal innervation to expiratory and inspiratory muscles in that motor neurons supplying expiratory muscles are inactive when motor neurons supplying inspiratory muscles are active, and vice versa.

 

Inspiration
Initiation Pre-Botzinger complex (Pacemaker cells) in Medulla
Maintenance Apneustic center in lower Pons stimulates Dorsal group of neurons in the medulla
Termination  Apneustic center inhibited by Vagus and Pneumotaxic center


Regulation of expiration: During quiet breathing, expiration is a passive process; there is no firing of neurons. Ventral respiratory group of neurons are involved in forceful expiration like during exercise.

Mnemonic DIVE: Dorsal respiratory group for Inspiration and Ventral respiratory group for Expiration.





Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition, Page nos 646

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an example of feed forward control mechanism?

options.label: D
options.text: Exercise resulting in heart rate increase

questions.answerText: Exercise resulting in heart rate increase
questions.solutionHtml:
Exercise resulting in heart rate increase is not an example of feedforward control mechanism. However, thinking about exercise and it resulting in a heart rate increase would be an example of feedforward control mechanism.  

Feedforward control is that which makes an anticipatory or adaptive response without a specific stimulus.  

Temperature control - Thermoregulatory responses are initiated by the hypothalamus before the changes in environmental temperature changes the core body temperature. Thus, shivering in response to cold environment would be an example of feedforward control.

In the cephalic phase of gastric secretion, the thought of food itself and not food per se produces a gastric secretion.

The cerebellum has a feed-forward inhibition that limits the duration of the excitation produced by any given afferent volley.





Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition, Page nos 129, 245
Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Page no. 9, 10

questions.stem: Single breath nitrogen method is used for measuring ____
questions.solutionHtml:
Anatomical dead space can be measured by the single-breath N2 curve (Fowler's method).

  • Anatomical dead space is the respiratory system volume exclusive of alveoli.
  • Alveolar dead space is the volume of gas not equilibrating with blood i.e. wasted ventilation.
  • Physiological/total dead space is the sum of anatomical and alveolar dead space.
  • The equation used for the calculation of total/physiological dead space is the Bohr’s equation.


The patient takes a deep breath of O2 From mid-inspiration, then exhales steadily. The changes in the N2 concentration of expired gas during expiration are plotted.

Region I - Dead Space (DS)

From I–II is a mixture of DS and alveolar gas.

The transition from III-IV is the closing volume (CV).

End of IV - Residual Volume (RV).

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones is exclusively secreted by adrenal gland but not by the ovaries of females?
questions.solutionHtml:
DHEAS is exclusively secreted from the adrenals but not by ovaries because ovaries lack the enzyme dehydroepiandrosterone-sulphotransferase needed to form DHEAS. 

90% of DHEA is synthesised by the adrenals and 10% comes from the ovaries.

questions.stem: Which hormone crosses the plasma membrane for its action?
questions.solutionHtml:
Thyroxine crosses the plasma membrane for its action.

Thyroid hormones enter the nucleus and bind to thyroid hormone receptors. The hormone-receptor complex in the nucleus binds to DNA via zinc fingers. This increases the expression of a variety of different genes that code for proteins regulating cell function.  Although thyroxine is an AA derivative, there are transporters to move it into the cell, hence they are intracellular receptors acting on the nucleus.

Epinephrine, glucagon, and insulin bind to cell surface receptors.





Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page nos 296 and 362
Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page no: 998

questions.stem: Afferent fibers from baroreceptors for blood pressure control goes to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Afferent fiber for blood pressure control goes to the Nucleus Tractus Solitarius (NTS).

Increased BP stimulates the baroreceptors which provide negative feedback in response to the increase in blood pressure.

Baroreceptor reflex:

  • Increased BP → stimulation of baroreceptors → stimulation of NTS → excitation of CVLM → inhibition of RVLM → inhibition of sympathetic system
  • Stimulation of NTS also stimulates CVC → parasympathetic stimulation
  • Net effect = sympathetic inhibition and parasympathetic stimulation → decreased HR and BP

NTS - Nucleus tractus solitarius

CVC - Cardiovagal centre

CVLM - Caudal ventrolateral medulla

RVLM - Rostral ventrolateral medulla

HR - Heart rate

BP - Blood pressure





Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition, Page nos 577 and 578

questions.stem: If the lung is allowed to undergo elastic recoil without the chest wall, the resultant volume of the lung would be?
questions.solutionHtml:
If lung is allowed to undergo elastic recoil without the chest wall, the resultant volume of the lung would be minimum volume as the opposing force by the chest wall would be non existant. 



The yellow line in the above graph denotes the compliance of lungs alone. According to the graph, when the pressure (x axis)  inside the lung is zero, there is some volume of air lesser than FRC still present (y axis) inside the lungs which is less than the functional residual capacity and residual volume which can be called as minimum volume.

questions.stem: You are an intern and want to determine the quantity of IV fluids needed for a patient. How much amount of transient loss/insensible loss per day would you account for in your calculations?
questions.solutionHtml:
500-600 ml of transient loss/insensible loss per day would have to be accounted for in the calculation.

Although water is lost through sweating especially in hot climates or during physical exertion, we tend to lose water at rest as well. Physiologically, water evaporates from the skin and lungs at a rate of about 600 to 700 ml/day. This is known as insensible water loss.





Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition, Pg no: 913

questions.stem: A soldier posted in Siachen is brought to you in the ER. In order to rule out hypothermia, how do you best measure his temperature?
questions.solutionHtml:
In the given clinical scenario rectal temperature would be the preferred site to measure the core body temperature.

During low or high temperatures like in Siachen, the axillary and the oral temperatures are highly misleading and should not be used to measure the core body temperatures

Infrared tympanic thermometer measures the temperature of the eardrum which is representative of core body temperature. However, more often the thermometer is not inserted adequately or for safety reasons, they are manufactured in such a way that they do not reach deep into the ear canal, or the ear canal contains cerumen which can disturb the measurement. Hence the infrared thermometer more commonly delivers the temperature of ear canal cerumen and hence not a reliable method of measuring the core body temperature.

questions.stem: "Vasopressin escape" in SIADH results due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Vasopressin escape in SIADH (Syndrome of inappropriate ADH secretion) results due to downregulation of aquaporin 2 production.

Prolonged exposure to elevated levels of vasopressin (ADH) leads eventually to downregulation of aquaporin-2 receptors. This prevents excessive reabsorption of water, despite high serum ADH levels and hence maintains euvolemia. This is known as vasopressin escape. This helps prevent excessive dilutional hyponatremia in SIADH. 





Ganong's Review Of Medical physiology, 26th Edition, Page no 688

questions.stem: Which of the following hormones do not act on the pancreas?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gastrin does not act upon the pancreas. Gastrin stimulates gastric acid secretion and gastric mucosal growth.
